Morning, George — it's Friday the fourteenth, and Athens is serving up more of the same: hot, dry, and blustery, low thirties with the Meltemi still charging in from the north, so fire risk's sitting high near the hills again.

— personal items —

Let's start with Colombia.

Remember that magnitude seven-point-four quake from Monday?

It's turned into one of the country's worst disasters in years.

The death toll's now past two hundred and seventy, with nearly four thousand injured and around three hundred and seventy still missing.

Rescuers are racing the clock in the western highlands, and the new government's thrown everything it has at the response.

Over in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers have besieged three Palestinian families in the village of Qusra for a fourth straight day, cutting off their water, power, and supplies.

It's a small, ugly flashpoint, but the kind that keeps the whole region simmering.

And your science note, a sobering one: a new Utrecht University study says the giant Atlantic current that keeps Europe mild — the AMOC — could actually collapse if warming arrives too fast.

The twist is that speed matters more than the number; warm slowly and the ocean adapts, warm quickly and it tips.

Early modelling, but a big deal if it holds up.

On the tech front, the big Western labs stayed quiet, but China's DeepSeek just shipped the full version of its V4 Pro model — and this one's worth your attention as a founder.

It's open-weight under a permissive license, so you can download it, fine-tune it on your own data, and run it yourself with no per-token bill to anyone.

It's a genuine frontier-class system built for coding and agent workflows, with a huge million-token context window, and it already plugs into tools like Claude Code.

Translation: open source is now nipping at the heels of the closed models — very good news for anyone building on a budget.

And as ever, any chatter about Google's next top-tier Gemini landing, treat it as rumour until it's actually live.

Around twenty-six first thing, up to about thirty-one by mid-afternoon, still in the high twenties come evening.

No rain, none in sight.

The Meltemi keeps blowing hard from the north — enough to buffet you around, nowhere near enough to cool you — and heat plus wind means fire risk stays elevated near the hills.

Sunset's a little after eight.

Quick health note: it's hot and bone dry, so keep a bottle close and sip early — doubly so if you're climbing.

On the gaming front, this week's free Epic game is Caravan SandWitch, a chilled sci-fi exploration thing where you roam a sun-baked, Provence-flavoured planet in a van hunting for your missing sister.

Yours to keep if you claim it before next Thursday, so no rush — just don't forget.

Finally, your learning bite.

Word of the day: deadpoint — in climbing, that's the split-second at the top of a dynamic move where you're briefly weightless, neither rising nor falling, and you snatch the hold at that dead moment.

And a productivity trick worth stealing: eat the frog.

Do your single hardest, most-dreaded task first thing, before the messages pile up — knock it out and the rest of the day feels downhill.

That's Friday — hot, windy, and quiet where it counts.

Grab your water, mind the sun, and have yourself an easy one.
